name: Eógan

attributes.attribute: fought Conn of the Hundred Battles

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Eógan is the Irish form of Owen. The name means yew tree. Several quasi-historical Irish kings bore this name. Eógan son of Ailill Olom founded the Eóganacht dynasty of the south. Eógan mac Néill founded the kingdom of Tyrone in Ulster. Eógan of Connacht asked to be buried upright for defense. Eógan Mór fought Conn of the Hundred Battles.
